key_insight: A nonstandard FEM-BEM coupling plus an H(curl)-conforming mixed formulation enables accurate whole-space simulation of the London equation and reveals that, in elongated ellipsoids, off-axis vortex paths can outperform the major axis in the isoflux problem.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical numerical framework for superconductivity design and analysis without artificial domain truncation, helping predict vortex nucleation behavior in complex 3D geometries.
method: Reformulate the magnetic field problem as a transmission problem for the potential in R^3.
Discretize the bounded/unbounded domains with a coupled FEM-BEM approach.
Compute B0 via Kikuchi’s mixed formulation using H(curl)-conforming elements.
evidence_signal: The authors report convergence tests validating the discretization and an application showing the expected diameter maximizer for a ball, plus numerical evidence of off-axis maximizers in sufficiently elongated ellipsoids.
watch_item: The off-axis maximizer result is numerical evidence rather than a proof, so implementation details and mesh resolution may affect the observed degeneracy in elongated geometries.
paper_title: Numerical approach to the London Equation of superconductivity
